summary: This was an open seat because Republican Gov. Kay Ivey was term-limited. Republican Tommy Tuberville, a U.S. senator, won, defeating Democrat Doug Jones, a former U.S. senator.

candidates.name: Tommy Tuberville
candidates.bio: Tommy Tuberville is a Republican who has been a U.S. senator from Alabama since January 2021. Before entering politics he was a college football coach, including head coach at Auburn University from 1999 to 2008.

positions.summary: Says he will lower taxes, cut waste and work with President Trump to reduce red tape and bring manufacturing jobs to Alabama.
Says he will back law enforcement and work with President Trump to deport illegal alien criminals.
Supports expanding school choice across charter, magnet, private, public and homeschool options, saying parents should be in charge of their child's education.
Says Alabama is a pro-life state and that no taxpayer dollars should go toward abortions.

candidates.name: Doug Jones
candidates.bio: Doug Jones is a Democrat who served as a U.S. senator from Alabama from 2018 to 2021. He was U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Alabama from 1997 to 2001 and later worked in private law practice.

positions.summary: Says he would fully eliminate the grocery tax and create a state Earned Income Tax Credit.
Says he would expand Medicaid to cover more than 154,000 working Alabamians and strengthen rural healthcare.
Says he would expand childcare options and provide free community college for adults without credentials.
Said in 2017, during his Senate campaign, that abortion is a woman's intensely personal decision and that he stands with Planned Parenthood.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called) Original summary noted the result was based on unofficial results.
